sources.sourceContract: league schedule -> team schedule -> team game number -> Strat game ID -> box score + play-by-play

frozenPreviewComparison.reason: No certified immutable pre-series snapshot exists for Games 70-72. Historical preview performance must not be reconstructed as if known pre-series.

seriesOutcome.interpretation: Aquarium won the series 2-1 despite a negative aggregate run differential driven by the 15-0 Game 71 outlier.

findings: Dean Chance completed 9 innings, allowing 6 hits and 1 earned run.
Aquarium led only 3-1 through seven before scoring four runs in the eighth.
Chance completed the game, preserving the bullpen for the remainder of the series.
Aquarium produced 14 hits with broad offensive contribution rather than dependence on one hitter.
games.managerialAssessment: Strong starter management and maximum bullpen preservation.

findings: Norwich scored five runs in the second inning after Washburn recorded the first two outs.
Washburn finished with 1.2 innings and 5 earned runs; the practical hook window developed rapidly during a two-out rally.
Jerry Nyman stopped the second-inning rally but was pinch-hit for because his batting position arrived in a no-DH game with Aquarium trailing 5-0.
John Boozer absorbed 2 innings and 8 earned runs as the game became noncompetitive.
Aquarium created baserunners but failed to convert six hits and three walks into a run.
Duke Sims drove in six Norwich runs.
Premium late-game bullpen resources were not consumed attempting to reduce the margin of an effectively lost game.
games.managerialAssessment: Tactically ugly but strategically defensible bullpen-resource preservation after the game became noncompetitive.

findings: Aquarium entered the seventh inning trailing 5-3.
With two outs, Al Spangler hit a two-run triple to tie the game.
Jim Fregosi followed with the go-ahead RBI single against Jeff James.
Darold Knowles pitched a perfect seventh inning after Aquarium took the lead.
Knowles was then pinch-hit for in the eighth, reflecting the no-DH pitcher-slot tradeoff.
Steve Hamilton pitched the final two innings, allowing one hit and no runs.
Knowles and Hamilton combined for three scoreless leverage innings after being preserved during the Game 71 blowout.
Duke Sims was injured for three additional games; Jake Gibbs replaced him and produced a two-run single in the current game.
games.managerialAssessment: Strong comeback management and excellent conversion of preserved bullpen resources into high-leverage outs.

learnedSignals.finding: Bullpen availability has series-level value. Preserving premium relievers in a noncompetitive game can directly improve the probability of converting a later close game.
learnedSignals.evidence: Chance preserved the bullpen in Game 70; lower-leverage arms absorbed the Game 71 blowout; Knowles and Hamilton then produced three scoreless leverage innings in the 6-5 Game 72 win.
learnedSignals.futureUse: Future previews and in-series decisions should show reliever freshness and cross-game resource value, not only season ERA and static bullpen role.

learnedSignals.finding: Final score alone is insufficient to describe how a game was decided.
learnedSignals.evidence: The three games represented starter domination with late breakaway, a two-out collapse followed by resource preservation, and a two-out comeback followed by a bullpen lock.
learnedSignals.futureUse: Classify completed games by shape and expose the decisive transition rather than relying on final margin.

learnedSignals.finding: Pitcher-hook evaluation must measure when actionable deterioration became visible, not judge solely from the final pitching line.
learnedSignals.evidence: Washburn reached two outs with nobody on in the second before the five-run rally developed rapidly.
learnedSignals.futureUse: Evaluate hook opportunities event-by-event using score, outs, baserunners, pitcher deterioration, bullpen state, and series context.

learnedSignals.finding: Two-out inning extension materially influenced multiple decisive innings in this series.
learnedSignals.evidence: Norwich created the five-run Game 71 second after two outs; Norwich also extended the Game 72 sixth with two outs; Aquarium scored all three decisive Game 72 seventh-inning runs after two outs.
learnedSignals.futureUse: Track two-out baserunners, runs, inning extensions, and damage allowed as a distinct recent-series signal while governing against overreaction to small samples.

learnedSignals.finding: Baserunner creation and run conversion should be measured separately.
learnedSignals.evidence: Aquarium produced six hits and three walks in the 15-0 loss but scored zero, while Game 72 converted traffic into the decisive rally.
learnedSignals.futureUse: Separate offensive opportunity creation from sequencing/conversion when diagnosing recent performance.

learnedSignals.finding: A single extreme blowout should remain visible as downside-tail evidence without dominating series-level evaluation.
learnedSignals.evidence: Norwich outscored Aquarium 21-14 across the series, but Aquarium won two of three games.
learnedSignals.futureUse: Preserve extreme losses as volatility/risk evidence while weighting individual game shape and series outcome separately.

learnedSignals.finding: Duke Sims was injured for three additional games in Game 72.
learnedSignals.evidence: The Game 72 play-by-play explicitly recorded the injury following a hit-by-pitch.
learnedSignals.futureUse: Retain as short-lived opponent availability intelligence only; revalidate against the live injury source before any future Norwich matchup.

learnedSignals.finding: Team schedule game numbers must not be equated with league-scoped Strat game IDs.
learnedSignals.evidence: Aquarium Games 70-72 resolved to Strat game IDs 417, 423, and 429.
learnedSignals.futureUse: Always resolve game identity through /league/schedule/{leagueId}, then team schedule, then actual Strat game ID before box-score or play-by-play ingestion.

governance.shortSamplePolicy: Recent-series signals may create watch items, questions, and resource-state intelligence. They must not be promoted into stable performance rates from one three-game series.
governance.outlierPolicy: Extreme single-game outcomes remain downside-tail evidence but must not overwrite broader series or season evidence.
governance.nextPreviewPolicy: This learning may inform future Series Previews created after this artifact. It must not be injected retroactively into the already-frozen Games 73-75 Hogs preview.
